deviations: The normal syncLibraryFromSessions batch keeps its original whole-batch writer lease so CLI organization and other atomic batch consumers cannot observe a half-applied collection; only the explicit startup chunk API permits one-session lease boundaries.
Sources modified within five minutes are scheduled through the dedicated live worker immediately after a successful writer probe; only the newest physical path per logical session is selected.
Each startup boundary joins already-running live work and forces at most two additional round-robin keys through their cutoff generations; post-cutoff events stay queued for later boundaries.
Root switching remains paused until the new root is initialized; its deferred source events are replayed after the root epoch transition instead of writing across roots.
knownRisks: The final composed candidate still needs the parent integrator to rerun the real recovered Library 60-second gate; this worktree never touched the running app or real Library.
The 100MB performance acceptance used a synthetic isolated Claude JSONL with the same byte scale, not the user's private Codex transcript.
Native Windows event delivery and filesystem performance were not exercised on this macOS host.
rootCause: Startup worker.sync serialized every later session-sync request behind one requestTail.
syncLibraryFromSessions held one maintenance lease across the entire approximately 1800-session startup batch.
A source event observed while libraryInitialized was false permanently captured maintainLibrary=false, so it parsed and indexed after startup but never updated Library.

The first f3b1697 implementation replaced the full-batch wait with waitForIdle at every startup boundary; continuous events below the quiet window could rearm forever, so independent audit correctly blocked it for startup starvation.

independentAudit.finding: Unbounded waitForIdle could prevent Library initialization from ever reaching ready under a continuously active source.
R2 uses bounded cutoff generations, persistent round-robin key history, joins in-flight work, and defers ordinary queue draining until startup establishes its next chunk boundary.
